exposition_seals.compressed_statement: For positive integer n, positive real β,λ and every real y, set ρ(t)=exp(-1/t) for t>0 and 0 otherwise, k(s)=ρ(2-|s|)/(ρ(2-|s|)+ρ(|s|-1)), φ(t)=the oriented integral of k from 0 to t, and U(y)=(nβ²/λ)φ(λy/(nβ)).

lossless_expansion.formula: The two ρ arguments sum to 1, so the denominator is positive. With z=2-|s| and 1-z=|s|-1 the quotient is smoothUnitCutoff(s), not a replacement by a merely similar function.

lossless_expansion.formula: Integrate k on 0..λy/(nβ) with signed endpoints, then multiply by nβ²/λ. All real y, including zero and negative values, are in domain; no fallback values or choice of primitive.

exposition_seals.independent_confirmation: The paired theorem statement specifies piecewise ρ, and the prerequisite's formula and exact body retain both branches, endpoints and scales. exposition_seals.compressed_statement: With U the literal positive-parameter load above, a fixed a∈[0,1], and Y on any measurable probability space with law N(0,v), v≥0, exp(-aU(Y)) is integrable and its expectation is at most exp(β² Var_P(Y)/2). Both gate endpoints and the degenerate law are included.

lossless_expansion.formula: Even k∈[0,1] makes φ(-t)=-φ(t) and |φ(t)|≤|t| by signed interval calculus and integration of 1 over the unordered comparison interval. FTC supplies continuity; no supplied measurability.
Positive scaling preserves continuity and oddness; (nβ²/λ)·|λy/(nβ)|=β|y| exactly, including y=0.

The established load satisfies the Gaussian envelope/symmetry/cosh/MGF argument. Pushforward equality and a.e. measurability transport actual integrability and the integral to P; Var_P(Y)=v identifies the exact RHS, including v=0.

exposition_seal.compressed_statement: For a Borel measurable odd U:ℝ→ℝ satisfying |U(y)|≤β|y| at every real y, fixed a∈[0,1], and centered Gaussian law N(0,v) with v≥0, exp(-aU) is integrable and its integral is at most exp(β²v/2). The envelope forces β≥0; neither β>0 nor v>0 is assumed.

lossless_expansion.formula: Measurable exponential terms of both signs are dominated by exp(βy)+exp(-βy) using |aU(y)|≤|βy|. The two Gaussian terms are integrable. This discharges the source-implicit integration bridge, not a source repair or added premise.
Gaussian reflection and oddness equate the two integrals, which can be averaged since both are integrable. Their average is the cosh integral; the argument also applies at v=0.
Cosh is monotone in the absolute argument, so cosh(aU)≤cosh(βy); the signed Gaussian MGF values average to exp(β²v/2), retaining the exact 1/2 and no factor-of-two loss.

exposition_seal.independent_confirmation: The equations and Lean drill-down preserve all hypotheses, genuine integrability, degenerate variance and scalar scope.
